hypotheses.text: The primary clinical characterization cohort defining TAF4-related neurodevelopmental disorder (Janssen et al., 2022) comprises exactly n=8 individuals with de novo putative loss-of-function variants, wherein intellectual disability (HP:0001249), behavioral abnormalities (HP:0000708), and facial dysmorphisms (HP:0001999) each demonstrate a penetrance of at least 7/8 (87.5%).
hypotheses.rationale: Clinical delineation of novel dominant disorders requires establishing exact denominators and penetrance estimates across core phenotypic domains; Janssen et al. explicitly describe common features in their primary cohort of eight probands.

evidence.text: Janssen et al. (2022) established TAF4 as a dominant disease gene in a discovery cohort of eight individuals harboring heterozygous de novo pLoF variants, identifying intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms as core common manifestations.

source.title: De novo putative loss‐of‐function variants in TAF4 are associated with a neuro‐developmental disorder
source.quote: We here present a cohort of eight individuals, each carrying de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 and expressing phenotypes consistent with a neuro-developmental disorder (NDD). Common features include intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms.

hypotheses.text: Severe isolated developmental language disorder (HP:0002465 / HP:0060057) without global cognitive impairment (non-verbal IQ >= 70) represents an underrecognized mild manifestation of TAF4 haploinsufficiency, accounting for at least 1 individual in targeted sporadic DLD genome sequencing cohorts.
hypotheses.rationale: Kennis et al. (2026) report that monogenic causes of developmental language disorder include variants fitting the TAF4-related disorder spectrum, challenging the assumption that TAF4 pathogenic variants always produce global intellectual disability.

evidence.text: In a prospective cohort of 25 children with severe sporadic developmental language disorder and normal non-verbal intelligence (IQ >= 70), genome sequencing identified variants fitting the phenotypic spectrum of TAF4-related disorders.

hypotheses.text: Across all published primary T4NDD cohorts, individuals with de novo loss-of-function variants in TAF4 show absent or negligible rates (<5%) of major non-neurological structural malformations (e.g., craniosynostosis, complex congenital heart defects, or gut malrotations), differentiating T4NDD from other syndromic neurodevelopmental entities.
hypotheses.rationale: Correlating primary cohort series like Janssen et al. and syndromic screening studies like Timberlake et al. can establish whether structural cranial or internal organ anomalies form part of the canonical TAF4 spectrum or argue against it.

evidence.text: Large-scale trio exome sequencing of nonsyndromic craniosynostosis cohorts identified damaging de novo variants in loss-of-function intolerant genes driving neurocognitive deficits, but canonical craniosynostosis has not been described as a recurrent feature in primary T4NDD discovery cohorts.

new_directions.question_text: Which two unrelated patients were reported in 2021 according to OMIM entry #620450, and what are their specific HPO phenotype counts relative to the Janssen et al. series?
new_directions.rationale: Identifying this 2021 report referenced in OMIM #620450 will expand the total worldwide denominator of reported TAF4 probands and refine phenotype penetrance calculations.
